name: vscode-jisho
description: An offline Japanese dictionary in your sidebar: vocabulary and kanji search powered by JMdict, Kanjidic, and friends.
author: Drake Costa <drake@saeris.io> (https://saeris.gg)

scripts.build: vp pack && vp build && vp exec vsce package --no-yarn
scripts.build:platforms: vp pack && vp build && vp exec node scripts/package-platforms.ts
scripts.e2e: vp pack && vp build && vp exec playwright test
scripts.docs:shots: vp pack && vp build && vp exec playwright test e2e/docs
scripts.docs:claims: vp pack && vp build && vp exec playwright test e2e/docs/claims.docs.e2e.ts

vscode-jisho.highlighting.enabled.markdownDescription:
Color Japanese text by part of speech in your Markdown and plain-text files. It is a syntax highlighter for prose (verbs, nouns, particles, and auxiliaries each get their own color), making word boundaries visible.

This covers your own files only. For example sentences inside the Jisho panel, see `#vscode-jisho.appearance.colorExamples#`.

vscode-jisho.hover.enabled.description: Show a dictionary hover (reading, meanings, conjugation breakdown) over Japanese text in Markdown and plain-text files.

vscode-jisho.grammar.enabled.description: Explain grammar in hovers and the conjugation table: what a particle (は, を, に) does, and what an auxiliary (〜たい, 〜てしまう) adds to a conjugated verb. Turn off to keep hovers to dictionary definitions only.

vscode-jisho.appearance.textScale.description: Text size in the Jisho panel, as a multiplier over VS Code's font size. Kanji often need a little more room than Latin text.

enumDescriptions: Short English terms: noun, transitive, godan verb.
Japanese grammatical terms: 名詞, 他動詞, 五段動詞.
vscode-jisho.appearance.tagLabels.markdownDescription:
How to label the grammar tags on a word's page.

Japanese terms are what a textbook or a Japanese dictionary uses, and they are shorter, but only if you already read them. Either way, hovering a tag shows its full description.

vscode-jisho.appearance.colorExamples.markdownDescription:
Color the words in example sentences by part of speech, using the same palette as the grammar tags and the search breakdown.

This covers the Jisho panel only. To color Japanese in your own Markdown and plain-text files, see `#vscode-jisho.highlighting.enabled#`.

enumDescriptions: Nine distinct colors, one per part of speech.
Built for protanopia (reduced sensitivity to red).
Built for deuteranopia (reduced sensitivity to green), the most common form.
Built for tritanopia (reduced sensitivity to blue), which is rare.
vscode-jisho.appearance.palette.markdownDescription:
Which color palette to use when coloring Japanese by part of speech, in the panel and in the editor.

The three color-vision palettes are not tinted versions of the standard one. Each is built from scratch for how that type of vision actually perceives color, so words stay distinguishable rather than merely legible.

enumDescriptions: Direction arrows sit beside the stroke, leaving it visible while it draws.
Direction arrows trace the stroke's own path (Duolingo-style).
vscode-jisho.strokeOrder.guideStyle.description: How the stroke-order player draws its direction guides.

vscode-jisho.dictionary.autoCheck.description: Check once a day whether a newer dictionary is available and offer to update. Updates are never forced: you'll get a dismissible prompt. Run "Jisho: Check for Dictionary Updates" any time to check manually.

bumpy.buildCommand: vp pack && vp build && vp exec node scripts/package-platforms.ts
